cards.details: Written primarily Right-to-Left, switching to Left-to-Right in subsequent lines. Proven by sign compression on the left margins of seals.
Short inscriptions found on steatite seals, copper tablets, and clay pottery. The Dholavira Signboard features 10 large gypsum characters.

sections.title: 1. Characteristics, Decipherment Attempts & Writing Direction (Boustrophedon)
sections.content:
The Harappan script is a highly standardized system of graphic communication. While it has not been successfully deciphered, its structural characteristics are well documented.

Boustrophedon & Direction of Writing
  • Right-to-Left Start: The writing was primarily written from right to left. Scribes began on the right and compressed symbols on the left margin as they ran out of space (cramping).
  • Boustrophedon: Longer texts alternate directions. The first line runs right-to-left, the second left-to-right, mirroring the path of a plowing ox.
Script Typology & Sign Count

The script is **logo-syllabic**, meaning each sign represents a word or a syllable. It is not alphabetical (which would have ~30 signs) nor purely pictographic (which would have thousands). It features between **375 and 400 distinct signs**. Decipherment attempts are blocked because the language family is unknown, there are no bilingual inscriptions, and the average inscription length is very short (about 5 characters).

masteryZone.q: What is the primary archaeological evidence that the Harappan script was written from right to left?
opts: The compression or cramping of symbols on the left margin of seals
The alphabetical order starting with vowels on the right
The presence of bilingual plaques in Mesopotamia
The use of iron pens that left deep grooves on the right side
masteryZone.sol: The cramping of symbols on the left margin of seals proves the scribe ran out of space when writing from right to left.

masteryZone.q: The total number of distinct signs identified in the Indus script is estimated to be between:
masteryZone.sol: Mainstream concordances identify between 375 and 400 distinct symbols in the script.

masteryZone.q: The term 'Boustrophedon' writing system refers to:
opts: Writing that is carved only on stone structures
Writing that alternates direction from line to line
A script that uses only animal-themed pictographs
A system read vertically from bottom to top
masteryZone.sol: Boustrophedon literally means 'ox-turning' and refers to text alternating directions line-by-line.

masteryZone.q: Linguistically, the Harappan script is best categorized as a:
masteryZone.sol: It is logo-syllabic, where signs represent both words (logograms) and phonetic syllables.

masteryZone.q: What is the average number of signs found in a standard Harappan inscription?
masteryZone.sol: The average inscription length is extremely short, about 5 signs, with the longest containing 26.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following indicate that the Indus script was written from right to left? (Select all that apply)
opts: Cramping of signs on the left margins of seals
Overlapping strokes on pottery incisions where left strokes overlap right ones
Symmetric designs that can only be carved from the right side
Bilingual translations engraved on Mesopotamian boundary stones
masteryZone.sol: Left margin cramping and overlapping pottery strokes prove right-to-left writing direction.

masteryZone.q: Select the structural characteristics of the Harappan logo-syllabic script: (Select all that apply)
opts: Too many signs for an alphabet but too few for a pictographic system
Each character represents a word or a syllable
Lacks any abstract geometric shapes, using only animal drawings
masteryZone.sol: The script has 375-400 signs, is logo-syllabic, and contains many abstract geometric symbols.

masteryZone.q: Why has the decipherment of the Indus script remained unsuccessful? (Select all that apply)
opts: Lack of any bilingual inscription like the Rosetta Stone
Unknown language family of the Harappan civilisation
Extreme brevity of the recovered inscriptions
Complete absence of any computerized concordances
masteryZone.sol: Decipherment is blocked by the lack of bilingual texts, unknown language family, and brief texts. Computer concordances do exist.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following directions of writing are observed in Harappan inscriptions? (Select all that apply)
opts: Right to left in single-line inscriptions
Top-to-bottom vertical columns in all seals
Left-to-right starting from the middle of the seal
masteryZone.sol: Writing is right-to-left in single lines and alternates (Boustrophedon) in multi-line texts.

masteryZone.q: Identify the common graphic representations found in the script symbols: (Select all that apply)
opts: Fish symbols with various modifying strokes
Human-like figures carrying bows or sticks
Exclusively Roman numerals and mathematical signs
masteryZone.sol: Fish signs, jar signs, and human-like figures are common; Roman numerals did not exist.

masteryZone.q: The Harappan script was a highly simplified alphabetical writing system consisting of 26 letters.
masteryZone.sol: It was logo-syllabic with 375-400 signs, not alphabetic.

masteryZone.q: The longest single inscription discovered in the Indus valley contains exactly 26 signs.
masteryZone.sol: True. The longest inscription, found on a seal or pottery sherd, contains 26 characters.

masteryZone.q: Boustrophedon writing style involves alternating directions of writing in consecutive lines.
masteryZone.sol: True. The text alternates: line 1 goes right-to-left, line 2 left-to-right, etc.

masteryZone.q: Sign cramping on the left margin of seals suggests that writing started from the left.
masteryZone.sol: False. Cramping on the left shows the writer ran out of space as they moved from right to left.

masteryZone.q: Archaeologists have found bilingual tablets in Harappa written in both Indus script and Sumerian cuneiform.
masteryZone.sol: False. No bilingual inscriptions have ever been found for the Indus script.

masteryZone.q: The 'fish' sign is one of the most common symbols in the Harappan script.
masteryZone.sol: True. The fish sign appears frequently and with several variants.

masteryZone.q: A concordance is a systematic compilation of all script signs, their variants, and positions.
masteryZone.sol: True. Concordances compiled by Mahadevan and Parpola are major resources for scholars.

masteryZone.q: There is direct evidence of paper or papyrus sheets being used by Harappan scribes.
masteryZone.sol: False. No direct evidence of writing on organic paper or papyrus has survived.

masteryZone.q: The writing direction that alternates from right-to-left and left-to-right is called ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Boustrophedon is the term for alternating writing direction.

masteryZone.q: The total count of distinct characters in the Harappan script ranges between ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Concordances list between 375 and 400 unique signs.

masteryZone.q: The compression of characters occurs on the ___________ margin of steatite seals.
masteryZone.sol: Cramping is observed on the left margin, proving right-to-left writing.

masteryZone.q: A script in which characters stand for words or syllables is called ___________.
masteryZone.sol: The logo-syllabic script uses signs for words and syllables.

masteryZone.q: The longest known Indus inscription contains a sequence of ___________ signs.
masteryZone.sol: The longest inscription has 26 characters.

masteryZone.q: The graphic symbol resembling a ___________ is the most frequently occurring sign.
masteryZone.sol: The fish symbol is the most common graphic sign.

masteryZone.q: The decipherment of the Indus script is blocked by the absence of a ___________ text.
masteryZone.sol: No bilingual Rosetta-like stone has been found.

masteryZone.q: Overlapping incisions on pottery ___________ verify that right-to-left lines were drawn first.
masteryZone.sol: Overlapping lines on pottery graffiti confirm the right-to-left direction.

masteryZone.q: Match the writing terminology with its description:

options.text: A. Alternating writing direction line by line
B. Signs representing words or syllables
C. Systematic catalog of script symbols and occurrences

masteryZone.sol: Boustrophedon is alternating direction, logo-syllabic represents words/syllables, and concordance is the catalog.

masteryZone.q: Match the script statistics with their significance:

options.text: A. Count of distinct signs in the logo-syllabic script
B. Maximum signs in the longest single inscription
C. Average sign count in a standard inscription

masteryZone.sol: 375-400 signs, 26 is the longest text length, and 5 is the average text length.

masteryZone.q: Match the archaeological observation with its logical deduction:

items.left: I. Sign cramping on left margin
III. High number of unique signs

options.text: A. Scribe wrote from right to left
B. Right-hand strokes were carved first
C. Script is logo-syllabic rather than alphabetical

masteryZone.sol: Cramping proves right-to-left, overlapping proves right stroke first, and high sign count proves logo-syllabic.

masteryZone.q: What is the main direction of writing in single-line Indus inscriptions?
masteryZone.sol: From right to left.

masteryZone.q: What is the literal meaning of 'Boustrophedon'?
masteryZone.sol: Turning like an ox while plowing a field.

masteryZone.q: Why is the script termed logo-syllabic?
masteryZone.sol: Because the sign count is too high for an alphabet and too low for pure pictography, representing words and syllables.

masteryZone.q: What is the maximum length of a single continuous inscription found?
masteryZone.sol: 26 signs.

masteryZone.q: What evidence on pottery sherds confirms right-to-left writing?
masteryZone.sol: Overlapping lines where the stroke on the left overrides the stroke on the right.

masteryZone.q: Has the Harappan script been deciphered?
masteryZone.sol: No, it remains undeciphered.

masteryZone.q: Which graphic symbol is most frequently repeated in the script?
masteryZone.sol: The fish symbol.

masteryZone.q: What key archaeological discovery is missing that would easily help decipher the script?
masteryZone.sol: A bilingual inscription (like the Rosetta Stone).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Harappan script was written from right to left.
Reason (R): Inscriptions on steatite seals show sign cramping on their left margins.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The Harappan script is classified as alphabetical.
Reason (R): The script contains between 375 and 400 distinct signs, which matches the size of an alphabet.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is false and R is false (the high sign count proves it is logo-syllabic, not alphabetical).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Long Harappan inscriptions are written in the Boustrophedon style.
Reason (R): Scribes always started every line on the left margin and wrote towards the right.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is true but R is false (Boustrophedon alternates directions rather than starting on the left).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Mainstream scholars agree that the Indus script has not been successfully deciphered.
Reason (R): There is no bilingual inscription to provide a key for translating the characters.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Scribes carved the characters on seals in reverse (mirror-image).
Reason (R): The seals were designed to stamp clay sealings, which would display the correct reading orientation.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): The average length of Indus inscriptions is about 50 signs.
Reason (R): The longest single inscription found contains only 26 signs.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is false because average length is 5 signs. R is true.

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Pottery graffiti overlaps confirm the writing direction.
Reason (R): Leftward strokes were carved before rightward strokes, showing a left-to-right flow.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: A is true but R is false (right strokes were carved first, confirming right-to-left flow).

masteryZone.q:
Assertion (A): Scribes used perishable materials for administrative books.
Reason (R): No administrative paper, palm leaves, or wood documents have survived in the archaeological record.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
masteryZone.sol: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the writing direction:
1. Single-line inscriptions were written from right to left.
2. The Boustrophedon style alternates directions in multi-line inscriptions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct, describing single-line and multi-line writing directions.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the number of signs:
1. The Indus script contains fewer than 50 distinct characters.
2. The script is logo-syllabic in nature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: it contains 375-400 distinct signs, far more than 50.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding decipherment hurdles:
1. The discovery of bilingual seals in Sumeria resolved the translation of the script.
2. The longest Indus text contains 26 characters, which limits statistical decoding.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: no bilingual seals have been discovered.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding sign cramping:
1. Scribes cramped signs on the right margin of seals.
2. Scribes started writing from left to right on standard seals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Neither statement is correct. Cramping is on the left margin, showing right-to-left writing.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the fish symbol:
1. The fish symbol is the most frequently occurring sign in the script corpus.
2. The symbol is often modified with strokes or fins to represent different values.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct, describing the frequency and modifications of the fish symbol.

masteryZone.q: Why did Harappan scribes compress their letters on the left margin of seals?
masteryZone.sol: Because they wrote from right to left and miscalculated the space remaining as they approached the left margin.

masteryZone.q: Why is a bilingual inscription necessary to decipher an unknown script like the Indus script?
masteryZone.sol: It provides a parallel translation in a known language, allowing scholars to map known words and phonetics directly to the unknown signs.

masteryZone.q: Why is the script called logo-syllabic instead of alphabetical?
masteryZone.sol: Because the sign count of 375-400 is too large to represent individual alphabetic sounds, but too small for purely pictographic words, representing both words and syllables.

masteryZone.q: How did epigraphers prove the right-to-left writing direction of the script?
masteryZone.sol: By analyzing the physical crowding of signs on the left edge of seals and showing that incisions on the left overrode those on the right in pottery graffiti.

masteryZone.q: How does the Boustrophedon writing style change layout from line to line?
masteryZone.sol: It alternates directions: line 1 runs right-to-left, line 2 curves down and runs left-to-right, line 3 runs right-to-left, and so on.

masteryZone.q: How did mirror-image carving of seals relate to their practical usage?
masteryZone.sol: Seals were carved in reverse so that when pressed into soft clay cargo tags, the resulting sealing impression would display the symbols in their correct, readable format.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: An archaeologist studies a steatite seal from Harappa and notices that the signs on the right are spaced widely, while the final two signs on the left are heavily cramped and overlapping. What deduction does this case study support?
masteryZone.sol: It supports the deduction that the seal was written from right to left, and that the scribe did not plan the spacing carefully beforehand.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: A newly found inscription contains a sequence of 26 symbols, making it the longest known Indus text. Scribes analyze it to find recurring grammatical patterns. Why does its length still hinder decryption?
masteryZone.sol: The text is still too short for statistical frequency analysis to isolate grammatical rules, syntax structures, or word combinations effectively.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Compare the decoding of Egyptian hieroglyphs using the Rosetta Stone with the Indus script. What is the key difference in availability that explains why one was solved and the other remains unsolved?
masteryZone.sol: Egyptian hieroglyphs had the Rosetta Stone with parallel Greek and Demotic text. The Indus script lacks any multi-lingual or bilingual texts, leaving no point of comparison.

masteryZone.q: Explain the concept of 'Boustrophedon' to a beginner using a simple analogy.
masteryZone.sol: Boustrophedon means writing like a bull plowing a field. Instead of lifting the pen and returning to the start of the line, the scribe writes the first line from right to left, then drops to the next line and writes left to right, matching the continuous path of the ox.

masteryZone.q: Explain why the Indus script is categorized as 'Logo-syllabic' and not alphabetical.
masteryZone.sol: An alphabet uses around 20-40 characters to represent individual sounds. A logo-syllabic script uses hundreds of signs (like the Indus script's 375-400 signs) because each symbol represents a whole word (logogram) or a syllable sound, rather than a single letter.

masteryZone.q: Explain the phenomenon of 'Sign Cramping' and how it acts as evidence of writing direction.
masteryZone.sol: Sign cramping occurs when a scribe begins writing on one side of a seal and runs out of physical space as they reach the other edge, causing the final signs to be squished together. In Harappan seals, this squishing is consistently on the left, proving writing began on the right.

sections.title: 2. Key Archaeological Inscriptions (Seals, Copper Tablets & Dholavira Signboard)
sections.content:
The Harappan script is found across multiple physical mediums, reflecting its administrative, trade, and civic integration in daily municipal life.

Steatite Seals & Copper Inscriptions
  • Steatite Seals: The majority of writing is found on square steatite seals, where short texts accompany animal reliefs (unicorn, bull) to stamp clay cargo tags.
  • Copper Tablets: Small copper plates feature engraved script signs on one side and animal figures on the other, likely serving as trade tokens or amulets.
The Dholavira Signboard

Discovered at Dholavira, Gujarat, this unique inscription features **ten large symbols**, each about 37 cm high. The signs were carved out of white gypsum crystalline paste and mounted on a large wooden board that once hung over the northern gateway of the Citadel. This indicates that writing had public administrative utility, declaring civic authority to visitors.

masteryZone.q: At which Harappan site was the famous public 'Signboard' inscription discovered?
masteryZone.sol: The ten-sign signboard was discovered at Dholavira in Gujarat.

masteryZone.q: The large symbols of the Dholavira Signboard were manufactured using which material?
masteryZone.sol: The letters were shaped out of white gypsum crystalline paste and mounted on wood.

masteryZone.q: On what class of objects are the vast majority of Harappan script inscriptions found?
masteryZone.sol: Steatite seals constitute the single largest category of objects bearing Indus writing.

masteryZone.q: Inscriptions on Indus copper tablets typically feature script signs on one side and what on the other?
masteryZone.sol: Copper tablets typically carry script on one side and an animal image (e.g., unicorn) on the reverse.

masteryZone.q: What was the primary function of the steatite seals containing script and animal reliefs?
opts: To serve as currency in daily transactions
To stamp clay tags (sealings) to secure trade goods
To act as religious gravestones in cemeteries
masteryZone.sol: Seals were stamped on wet clay sealings (tags) to secure packages and identify ownership in trade.

masteryZone.q: On which of the following media has the Harappan script been discovered? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Indus writing is found on seals, copper tablets, pottery, and ivory rods.

masteryZone.q: Select the key details regarding the Dholavira Signboard: (Select all that apply)
opts: Mounted above the northern gateway of the Citadel
Deciphered as a tax warning to visiting traders
masteryZone.sol: The board has 10 signs, is 37 cm high, and was at the Citadel northern gate. It is undeciphered.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following functions did steatite seals perform? (Select all that apply)
opts: Securing goods during long-distance maritime trade
Identifying merchant ownership or clan identity
Serving as amuletic charms for protection
Serving as uniform legal coinage across the empire
masteryZone.sol: Seals secured goods, showed identity, and acted as amulets. They were not coinage.

masteryZone.q: Identify the features of Indus copper tablets: (Select all that apply)
opts: Found primarily at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa
Feature animal drawings on one side
Engraved with script signs on the other side
Used as physical mirrors for elite makeup
masteryZone.sol: Copper tablets have script and animals, found at Mohenjo-daro and Harappa. Mirrors were polished bronze plates, not tablets.

masteryZone.q: What findings confirm that writing was used by ordinary citizens, not just administrative elites? (Select all that apply)
opts: Post-firing graffiti scratched on domestic potsherds
Inscribed pottery found in commoners' Lower Town residential areas
Terracotta bangles carrying tiny stamped script signs
Large gold plaques with legal decrees found in slums
masteryZone.sol: Pottery graffiti and inscribed Lower Town artifacts show ordinary use. Gold plaques do not exist.

masteryZone.q: The Dholavira Signboard was recovered from the southern gate of the Citadel.
masteryZone.sol: It was found near the northern gateway of the Citadel at Dholavira.

masteryZone.q: The letters of the Dholavira Signboard were made of white gypsum.
masteryZone.sol: True. Crystalline gypsum paste was used to make the letters.

masteryZone.q: Steatite (soapstone) was the primary raw material used for making Harappan seals.
masteryZone.sol: True. Steatite was preferred because it was soft to carve and hardened when fired.

masteryZone.q: Every single Indus seal discovered has a script inscription on it.
masteryZone.sol: False. Some seals only have animal figures or geometric designs without any script.

masteryZone.q: Copper tablets containing script are found in large quantities in almost every Harappan village.
masteryZone.sol: False. They are concentrated in major metropolitan sites like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa.

masteryZone.q: Indus script signs have been found scratched on terracotta bangles.
masteryZone.sol: True. Some bangles have tiny script stampings or scratchings.

masteryZone.q: The wood backing of the Dholavira Signboard decayed over time, leaving the gypsum inlays in the soil.
masteryZone.sol: True. The wooden frame rotted away, but the gypsum symbols fell and survived in the dirt.

masteryZone.q: Writing on pottery was exclusively executed before the pots were baked in the kiln.
masteryZone.sol: False. Much of it was post-firing graffiti, scratched onto the baked pots by their owners.

masteryZone.q: The public signboard containing ten large characters was discovered at ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Dholavira yielded the famous public signboard.

masteryZone.q: The crystalline material used to shape the signboard characters was ___________.
masteryZone.sol: The letters were made of gypsum paste.

masteryZone.q: Most Indus valley seals were made from a soft stone called ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Steatite (or soapstone) was the primary material for seals.

masteryZone.q: The Dholavira Signboard consists of exactly ___________ large symbols.
masteryZone.sol: The signboard contains 10 letters.

masteryZone.q: Engraved copper plates carrying signs and animals likely served as ___________ or amulets.
masteryZone.sol: Copper tablets likely acted as identity tokens or amulets.

masteryZone.q: Markings scratched onto pottery after it has been baked are known as ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Post-firing scratchings on pottery are called graffiti.

masteryZone.q: Tiny inscriptions have also been discovered on ___________ rods used for gaming or scaling.
masteryZone.sol: Ivory rods carry miniature script signs.

masteryZone.q: The clay impressions left by pressing seals into wet clay are called ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Sealings are the clay impressions of seals.

masteryZone.q: Match the inscribed objects with their primary materials:

options.text: A. Gypsum paste inlays
B. Steatite (soapstone)
C. Ivory (elephant tusk)

masteryZone.sol: Signboard is gypsum, seals are steatite, and gaming rods are ivory.

masteryZone.q: Match the sites with their distinct epigraphic discoveries:

options.text: A. Ten-character gateway signboard
B. Abundant copper tablets and seals
C. Clay sealings on warehouse packages

masteryZone.sol: Dholavira has the signboard, Mohenjo-daro has copper tablets, and Lothal has warehouse sealings.

masteryZone.q: Match the archaeological object with its trade/civic function:

options.text: A. Tool used to imprint merchant identity
B. Medium to declare authority at city gates
C. Imprinted clay verifying cargo security

masteryZone.sol: Seal is the imprinting tool, signboard declares gate authority, and sealing verifies cargo security.

masteryZone.q: Where was the unique ten-sign public inscription found?
masteryZone.sol: Dholavira, Gujarat.

masteryZone.q: What is the approximate height of each gypsum letter on the Dholavira Signboard?
masteryZone.sol: 37 cm.

masteryZone.q: What mineral was soft enough to carve seals easily and hardened when heated?
masteryZone.sol: Steatite.

masteryZone.q: What was engraved on the reverse side of most Indus copper tablets?
masteryZone.sol: An animal figure (such as a unicorn or bull).

masteryZone.q: What civic message is the Dholavira Signboard believed to have conveyed?
masteryZone.sol: It represents a display of civic authority or city name at the Citadel entrance.

masteryZone.q: Where on the Citadel gates was the Dholavira Signboard originally hung?
masteryZone.sol: Over the northern gateway.

masteryZone.q: What is the term for markings scratched on pottery after baking?
masteryZone.sol: Post-firing graffiti.

masteryZone.q: Name a luxury material of animal origin that carries tiny script signs.
masteryZone.sol: Ivory (used for rods or combs).

masteryZone.q: Why did the gypsum letters of the Dholavira Signboard survive while the wood frame decayed?
masteryZone.sol: Because gypsum is an inorganic mineral paste that does not rot, whereas the wooden board was organic and decomposed in the soil over thousands of years.

masteryZone.q: Why were characters carved in reverse (mirror-image) on steatite seals?
masteryZone.sol: So that when the seal was pressed into wet clay tags, the resulting sealing impression would show the characters in their correct readable orientation.

masteryZone.q: Why was the Dholavira Signboard mounted publicly at the Citadel gate?
masteryZone.sol: To declare civic authority, rules, or the town's name to all incoming merchants and visitors, functioning as a monumental civic notice.

masteryZone.q: How did archaeologists recover and identify the Dholavira Signboard letters in the soil?
masteryZone.sol: By meticulously excavating the soil near the Citadel gate, identifying the aligned crystalline white gypsum shapes that sat in the soil where the wooden board had rotted away.

masteryZone.q: How were steatite seals utilized to secure merchant packaging during transport?
masteryZone.sol: A knot was tied on the cargo package, soft clay was placed over the knot, and the steatite seal was stamped onto the clay to create an authentic security seal.

masteryZone.q: How did post-firing graffiti on domestic pots differ from pre-firing stamps?
masteryZone.sol: Pre-firing stamps were pressed into wet clay before baking at a workshop, while post-firing graffiti was scratched by individual owners on finished baked pots to show possession.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Excavations at Lothal yielded a warehouse with dozens of clay tags showing seal impressions of unicorns and Indus script. None of the original wooden boxes survived. What trade practice does this study prove?
masteryZone.sol: It proves that seals were used to secure packaging and authenticate cargo during maritime transit, and that clay sealings survived even when the organic cargo boxes rotted.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The placement of the Dholavira Signboard at the northern gateway of the Citadel. If this signboard was meant for public view, what does this tell us about the literacy level or administrative nature of Dholavira?
masteryZone.sol: It indicates that either a portion of the population was literate or that visual symbols carried standardized public meanings, reflecting a highly organized municipal administration.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: A cache of copper tablets is discovered in a single house in Mohenjo-daro, with identical animal designs and text sequences. Why does this suggest they were tokens rather than unique seals?
masteryZone.sol: Because multiple copies of the exact same script and animal design were held together, showing they were mass-produced tokens, amulets, or standard trading passes rather than individual seals.

masteryZone.q: Explain the difference between a 'seal' and a 'sealing' to a student.
masteryZone.sol: A seal is the actual engraved stamp tool made of steatite or copper. A sealing is the clay impression left behind when the seal is pressed into soft wet clay on cargo packages to secure them.

masteryZone.q: Explain the significance of the Dholavira Signboard in the history of Indian writing.
masteryZone.sol: The Dholavira Signboard is the earliest known large-scale public civic inscription in India. It shows that writing was not just used for small private trade labels, but had public, monumental, and civic administrative applications.

masteryZone.q: Explain why pottery graffiti is highly valuable for understanding Harappan society.
masteryZone.sol: While seals are found in wealthy trading contexts, pottery graffiti is found on ordinary domestic pots in lower-class houses. This shows that basic knowledge or use of script symbols was widespread among common citizens, not just confined to elite merchants.

sections.title: 3. Linguistic Affiliation Theories (Dravidian, Indo-Aryan & Other Models)
sections.content:
In the absence of a decipherment key, scholars have proposed competing linguistic models to reconstruct the language spoken by the Indus people.

Dravidian & Indo-Aryan Hypotheses
  • Dravidian Model: Championed by Iravatham Mahadevan and Asko Parpola, this theory suggests the language belonged to the Proto-Dravidian family, linking symbols like the 'fish' sign (read as *min*) to Dravidian homophones.
  • Indo-Aryan Model: Proposed by S.R. Rao, this theory claims the script represents an early form of Sanskrit/Vedic Indo-Aryan, reading the signs alphabetically.
Non-Linguistic & Other Theories

Other scholars link the language to the Munda/Austroasiatic family. A major revisionist hypothesis by Steve Farmer, Richard Sproat, and Michael Witzel argues that the script did not encode a spoken language at all, acting instead as a **non-linguistic symbol system** of heraldic, clan, or ritual signs, citing the extreme brevity of the texts and lack of repeating markers.

masteryZone.q: Which Indian scholar is famous for compiling the first comprehensive computer concordance of the Indus script in 1977?
masteryZone.sol: Iravatham Mahadevan compiled the first comprehensive computer concordance of the script in 1977.

masteryZone.q: The leading Finnish scholar who has championed the Proto-Dravidian hypothesis of the Harappan language is:
masteryZone.sol: Asko Parpola is the foremost Finnish linguist supporting the Proto-Dravidian theory.

masteryZone.q: Which scholar proposed that the Harappan script was an alphabetical precursor to Sanskrit?
masteryZone.sol: S.R. Rao argued that the script was alphabetic and represented an early form of Indo-Aryan Sanskrit.

masteryZone.q: The Dravidian model reads the 'fish' sign as *min*, which homophonically represents both 'fish' and:
masteryZone.sol: In Dravidian languages, *min* means both fish and star, which is used to interpret astral signs on seals.

masteryZone.q: Who proposed the controversial revisionist theory that the Harappan script was a non-linguistic symbol system?
masteryZone.sol: Steve Farmer, Richard Sproat, and Michael Witzel proposed that the script did not encode a spoken language.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following scholars advocate for the Dravidian linguistic model of the Indus script? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Parpola, Mahadevan, and Fairservis support the Dravidian theory. S.R. Rao supports the Indo-Aryan theory.

masteryZone.q: Select the core arguments of the non-linguistic symbol hypothesis: (Select all that apply)
opts: Average text length is extremely short (4-5 signs)
Lacks the statistical sign repetitions expected in natural languages
Symbols acted as heraldic clan markers or ritual signs
The script has been proven to represent the Sumerian language
masteryZone.sol: Farmer, Sproat, and Witzel argue that brief texts, low repetition, and heraldic roles point to a non-linguistic system.

masteryZone.q: What are the major language families linked by various theories to the Harappan civilisation? (Select all that apply)
masteryZone.sol: Dravidian, Indo-Aryan, and Munda are the main proposed language families.

masteryZone.q: Why is S.R. Rao's Indo-Aryan/Sanskrit decipherment widely rejected? (Select all that apply)
opts: He assigned arbitrary phonetic values to signs to force Sanskrit readings
Mainstream linguists argue the script is logo-syllabic, not alphabetical
The grammar of Vedic Sanskrit does not match his translations
Sanskrit was proven to have originated in South America
masteryZone.sol: Rao's theory is rejected due to arbitrary values, alphabetical assumptions, and grammatical mismatch. Sanskrit did not originate in South America.

masteryZone.q: Which factors support the Dravidian hypothesis of the Harappan language? (Select all that apply)
opts: The survival of Brahui, a Dravidian language, in Baluchistan
Dravidian substratum elements found in early Rigvedic Sanskrit
The successful reading of the fish sign using Dravidian homophones
The discovery of Tamil inscriptions in Harappan ruins
masteryZone.sol: Brahui in Baluchistan, Dravidian influences in Rigveda, and Rebus readings support the Dravidian theory. No Tamil inscriptions have been found in Harappa.

masteryZone.q: Iravatham Mahadevan was a supporter of the Indo-Aryan hypothesis of the Harappan language.
masteryZone.sol: Mahadevan was a leading proponent of the Proto-Dravidian theory.

masteryZone.q: Asko Parpola utilized computers to study the sign distributions and support the Dravidian connection.
masteryZone.sol: True. Parpola did extensive computerized work to support the Dravidian theory.

masteryZone.q: The non-linguistic symbol theory states that the Harappan script was not a spoken language.
masteryZone.sol: True. The theory argues it was a system of heraldic and ritual symbols.

masteryZone.q: Brahui is a Dravidian language spoken in Baluchistan, near the Indus Valley region.
masteryZone.sol: True. Brahui provides geographical support for the Dravidian theory.

masteryZone.q: Munda languages belong to the Indo-European language family.
masteryZone.sol: False. Munda languages belong to the Austroasiatic language family.

masteryZone.q: S.R. Rao proposed that late Indus script signs evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.
masteryZone.sol: True. He argued for an evolutionary link from late Indus signs to Phoenician letters.

masteryZone.q: Linguists have reached a unanimous consensus that the Indus language was Dravidian.
masteryZone.sol: False. There is no consensus; it remains a matter of intense academic debate.

masteryZone.q: Entropy analysis compares the statistical order of script symbols with known languages.
masteryZone.sol: True. Computer entropy studies show Indus sign structures resemble natural languages.

masteryZone.q: The scholar who published the computer concordance of the Indus script in 1977 was ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Mahadevan compiled the 1977 concordance.

masteryZone.q: Asko Parpola is a leading proponent of the ___________ linguistic hypothesis.
masteryZone.sol: Parpola supports the Proto-Dravidian model.

masteryZone.q: The Indo-Aryan Sanskrit reading of the script was proposed by ___________ Rao.
masteryZone.sol: S.R. Rao proposed the Indo-Aryan alphabetical reading.

masteryZone.q: The non-linguistic symbol theory was published by Farmer, Sproat, and ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Steve Farmer, Richard Sproat, and Michael Witzel wrote the paper.

masteryZone.q: In Dravidian homophony, the word *min* represents both a fish and a ___________.
masteryZone.sol: Min stands for both fish and star.

masteryZone.q: The Munda languages belong to the ___________ language family.
masteryZone.sol: Munda is a branch of the Austroasiatic family.

masteryZone.q: Conditional ___________ is the mathematical metric used to prove the script has language-like order.
masteryZone.sol: Conditional entropy studies verify language-like ordering.

masteryZone.q: A linguistic pocket of Dravidian speakers surviving in Baluchistan is the ___________ language.
masteryZone.sol: Brahui is the Dravidian pocket in Baluchistan.

masteryZone.q: Match the scholars with their respective script theories:

options.text: A. Proto-Dravidian language hypothesis
B. Indo-Aryan Sanskrit hypothesis
C. Non-linguistic symbol system theory

masteryZone.sol: Parpola supports Dravidian, Rao supports Sanskrit, and Farmer supports the non-linguistic theory.

masteryZone.q: Match the terms with their definitions in script studies:

options.text: A. Using a pictograph of an object to represent a homophone
B. Systematic index of symbols across all texts
C. Statistical predictability of symbol sequences

masteryZone.sol: Rebus uses homophones, concordance is the systematic index, and entropy measures sequence predictability.

masteryZone.q: Match the language families with their connecting evidence:

options.text: A. Brahui language pocket in Baluchistan
B. Evolutionary arguments linking late Indus signs to Brahmi
C. Substratum Munda words in Rigveda

masteryZone.sol: Dravidian is linked to Brahui, Indo-Aryan to Brahmi evolution, and Austroasiatic to Rigvedic Munda words.

masteryZone.q: Who compiled the first comprehensive computer concordance of the Indus script in 1977?
masteryZone.sol: Iravatham Mahadevan.

masteryZone.q: Name the Dravidian language spoken in Baluchistan that supports the Dravidian hypothesis.
masteryZone.sol: Brahui.

masteryZone.q: Which Finnish scholar is famous for his work on the Dravidian decipherment of the script?
masteryZone.sol: Asko Parpola.

masteryZone.q: What is the core argument of the Farmer-Sproat-Witzel hypothesis?
masteryZone.sol: The script did not encode a spoken language but was a non-linguistic symbol system representing clans, status, or rituals.

masteryZone.q: Why is S.R. Rao's Sanskrit interpretation of the script widely rejected?
masteryZone.sol: Because it relies on arbitrary sign values and assumes a highly unlikely alphabetical system.

masteryZone.q: What Dravidian word homophonically represents both 'fish' and 'star'?
masteryZone.sol: *Min*.

masteryZone.q: What statistical method was used to prove the script has structured ordering similar to human language?
masteryZone.sol: Conditional entropy analysis.

masteryZone.q: What Munda-related language family is proposed as an alternative linguistic model?
masteryZone.sol: Austroasiatic.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Dravidian hypothesis:
1. Asko Parpola and Iravatham Mahadevan are leading scholars of this model.
2. It matches the geographic presence of the Dravidian-speaking Brahui pocket in Baluchistan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct and define the scholars and geographical support for the Dravidian model.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Indo-Aryan theories:
1. S.R. Rao proposed that the script was written alphabetically to encode Sanskrit.
2. His readings are universally accepted by Sanskrit scholars worldwide.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: his Sanskrit readings are widely rejected by mainstream scholars.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the non-linguistic symbol theory:
1. It was proposed by Farmer, Sproat, and Witzel in 2004.
2. It argues that the Indus script behaves statistically like road signs or heraldry rather than speech.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct, describing the proponents and core argument of the non-linguistic theory.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Munda linguistic connection:
1. Munda belongs to the Austroasiatic language family.
2. Substratum Munda words in the Rigveda suggest Munda speakers were present in Northwest India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Both statements are correct, detailing the Austroasiatic Munda family and Rigvedic substratum words.

masteryZone.q:
Consider the following statements regarding computer entropy analysis:
1. Entropy studies showed that the script has the exact same structure as random noise.
2. The sign sequences are entirely unordered, proving a non-linguistic nature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
masteryZone.sol: Neither statement is correct. Entropy studies showed the sign sequences are ordered and resemble natural human language systems, not random noise.

masteryZone.q: Why is the Brahui language of Baluchistan significant in debates about the Indus script?
masteryZone.sol: Because Brahui is a Dravidian language spoken in Baluchistan, proving that Dravidian languages were historically present in the northwest near the Indus Valley, supporting the Dravidian hypothesis.

masteryZone.q: Why did Steve Farmer and his co-authors claim the Indus script is non-linguistic?
masteryZone.sol: Because the inscriptions are extremely short (averaging 5 signs) with low repeat frequencies, lacking the length and repetition required to carry spoken grammar or sentences.

masteryZone.q: Why do linguists use the Rebus principle to interpret signs in a logo-syllabic script?
masteryZone.sol: Because a logo-syllabic script cannot easily draw abstract words, so it uses the picture of a concrete object that has the same spoken sound (homophone) as the abstract concept.

masteryZone.q: How does the Rebus principle work in interpreting the fish sign in the Dravidian model?
masteryZone.sol: The fish sign is read as Dravidian *min*. Since *min* also means star, the fish sign is interpreted to represent astral deities or stars on seals using homophonic substitution.

masteryZone.q: How did statistical analysis of conditional entropy challenge the non-linguistic theory?
masteryZone.sol: By calculating the probability of sign sequences, researchers found that the Indus script has a highly structured sign ordering that behaves like human language, rather than random symbols or coats-of-arms.

masteryZone.q: How does the Indo-Aryan hypothesis explain the connection between Harappan signs and historical Brahmi?
masteryZone.sol: Proponents argue that late Harappan symbols evolved into early Brahmi characters, suggesting a direct graphical transition and continuity of script in ancient India.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: The Brahui language of Baluchistan is surrounded by Indo-Aryan and Iranian languages. What historical linguistic process explains this island of Dravidian speakers, and how does it support Harappan theories?
masteryZone.sol: It is an enclave or remnant of a much larger prehistoric Dravidian-speaking area that once extended across Northwest India, suggesting the Indus Valley population spoke a Proto-Dravidian language.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Analyzing the 'fish' sign with six strokes. Under the Dravidian model, *min* (fish) plus the word for six (*aru*) translates homophonically to *aru-min*, meaning the Pleiades star cluster. What does this case study demonstrate?
masteryZone.sol: It demonstrates how Dravidian homophony (rebus writing) is used to translate abstract astronomical meanings from simple pictographic combinations on seals.

masteryZone.q: Case Study: Critique S.R. Rao's decipherment of the word 'eka-asva' (one horse) from a seal. Why did historical linguists point out that horses were not domestic staples in the Mature Harappan phase to reject his translation?
masteryZone.sol: Because his reading conflicted with the archaeological record, which shows that horses were not commonly domesticated or depicted in Mature Harappan culture, proving his translation was anachronistic.

masteryZone.q: Explain the 'Rebus Principle' of writing to a student using a modern English example.
masteryZone.sol: The Rebus Principle uses the picture of a word that sounds like another word to represent it. For example, to write the abstract message 'I can see you', you could draw pictures of an Eye (I), a tin Can (can), the Sea (see), and a female sheep or Ewe (you).

masteryZone.q: Explain the significance of the Brahui language pocket in Indus valley linguistic debates.
masteryZone.sol: Brahui is a Dravidian language spoken today in Baluchistan, Pakistan. Because it is thousands of miles away from other Dravidian languages in South India, it acts as a linguistic fossil, proving that Dravidian languages were once spoken in the Indus Valley region before being overtaken by Indo-Aryan languages.

masteryZone.q: Explain what a 'Concordance' is in the context of deciphering an ancient script.
masteryZone.sol: A concordance is a systematic index of all script signs. It catalogues every single inscription, listing which signs appear, their frequencies, what signs appear next to them, and on what materials. It allows scholars to analyze sign distribution mathematically without knowing the actual language.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the writing direction of the Harappan script:
1. Scribes wrote from right to left, as evidenced by the compression of symbols on the left margin of seals.
2. In longer inscriptions, they utilized the Boustrophedon system, where lines alternate in direction.
3. The writing direction of Boustrophedon is unique to the Harappan civilisation and is not found in any other ancient civilisation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: Boustrophedon writing is not unique to the Harappans; it is also found in early ancient Greek and Sabaean inscriptions.

practiceQuestions.q:
With reference to the nature of the Harappan script, consider the following statements:
1. It is a purely alphabetical script containing around 40 distinct characters.
2. The script is logo-syllabic, with each sign representing a word or a syllable.
3. The total number of identified distinct signs ranges between 375 and 400.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is incorrect: the script is logo-syllabic (375-400 signs), not alphabetical (which would require fewer than 40 characters).
